title: A business owner's legal remedies against defamatory online reviews
p1:
One bad review can damage years of hard work. But did you know that not every negative review gives a customer the right to say anything they want online?

Many business owners believe they simply have to accept false claims posted on review platforms.
p2: The surprising part is that a false statement presented as a fact can create legal issues. A genuine complaint about poor service is different from a review that knowingly spreads untrue allegations to harm a business reputation.
p3:
A business owner can respond by collecting evidence, requesting removal from the platform, and in serious cases, exploring legal remedies for defamation. The key is not to react emotionally but to document everything: screenshots, dates, customer records, and proof showing why the claim is false.

A professional response often protects credibility better than an angry reply.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a business receive an online review that crossed the line from criticism into defamation? What action should a business owner take?
